line: execute: async (id, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx) => run(await guest.ensure(ctx), id, params, signal, onUpdate),
reason: The seven routed tools reuse Pi's own built-in read, write, edit, bash, ls, find and grep definitions, schemas included, as the upstream gondolin example does. Pi validates every call against those TypeBox schemas before execute runs, and the built-in execute that receives the params validates them the same way. A zod mirror of seven schemas Pi owns would duplicate that check and could reject a call Pi accepts after a Pi upgrade.
/gondolin takes no arguments and ignores whatever follows it, as the upstream example does. Parsing the ignored text would reject nothing and add a schema with no input to guard.
